utterances.text: Haven't we heard an abundance of evidence, whether you agree with it or not, from other witnesses, here and there, that they actually saw people wearing HV uniforms with HV insignia? So what's the point of pursuing this information that one document out of a large bundle of documents says that there are reports that there are HV there but that they can't be confirmed because of certain reasons? We can take that on board and move on to something else. What is really important is for you to at some stage put to this witness that the Defence case will be and that you will prove that there were no HV units there at all at the operative time, but we really must come to that at some stage. I know that what you're doing with the documents is very useful to us, and I'm sure to your side, but eventually it has to lead you to the defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I absolutely agree with your thinking, Judge Clark. I just wanted, through these documents, to start on that topic and to start proving my case, because that was my intention and I wanted to clarify it through these documents. With the leave of the Trial Chamber, I would now proceed, and I'll try to make this as short as possible and use only the documents which are absolutely indispensable. Document number 62.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's in the second binder, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm looking at my notes, and I'll skip all the documents which relate to the Spanish battalion, because I believe that we got all of the information that we were able to get through another source, and I won't bother this witness with that. So we'll go straight on to document 66.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I ask you to turn to the last page of this document. Unfortunately, there is no French translation. So the last page, paragraph 13, one before last. To make this very brief, they say the troops were seen near Trilj. Buses were not sighted further to the north. My question is, do you know where the town of Trilj is located?

utterances.speaker: FRANCISCO AGUIRRE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me just repeat for the record, it's spelled as T-R-I-L-J, Trilj. Okay. There's no point in asking further questions about this document if you don't know where this town is. I'll move on to document 72. Certainly, if you like, I am conducting this exchange with you as a colleague, in that spirit. But with regard to this document, it was important for me whether you know where the town is located. If you want to make a comment on it, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: FRANCISCO AGUIRRE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am familiar with the area. Trilj must be a small town because I can't recall this name. But I can tell you where is the area because this can be seen from the other references in this paragraph. Because here, we see that Kamensko is mentioned, and Split is mentioned. Kamensko is the crossing point from the road that goes from Split to Tomislavgrad. So most likely Trilj is in this area. I wanted to mention this because Kamensko is also mentioned in other documents in this collection. It is an important border crossing point for the matter we are discussing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Distinguished colleague, since you have already voiced this comment, I would like you to look at the last sentence in this paragraph. The buses referred to above have not been sighted further north. Trilj is about 50 kilometres away from Imotski which is about 17 kilometres away from Sinj. That's where the town of Trilj is located. And they say that nothing had been sighted further north. Trilj is closer to Imotski in that direction, if that will help you place it. I don't want to waste more time bringing out maps. My colleague has just told me that the distance between Split and Trilj is the same as the distance between Trilj and the Bosnian border. So Trilj is halfway between Split and the Bosnian border. I would now like to move on to document 72. Since this is a UN document, I won't dwell on it. And I wouldn't ask you to comment on it because it regards the area of Vitez and what Izetbegovic or Tudjman would like in connection with it. I would like to ask you to move to binder number 3, Exhibit 492. So document 492, I think that is its identification number. It's an order by Mr. Petkovic and Mr. Stojic which says in one part of this order that Tuta is located in Bijelo Polje. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: FRANCISCO AGUIRRE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, can you help me; which part of the document?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Unfortunately, it's much harder for me to find because I don't have the documents marked in this binder. I don't have the tabs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, counsel took us to IAC 72. Was there no question on that, then?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So there's no -- okay. Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, because it was a UN document. I didn't want any comments on that from this witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise to the witness. It's very hard for me to find. I have to leaf through all these papers to get the number.

utterances.speaker: FRANCISCO AGUIRRE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean point 2, paragraph 1, 2-1?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I first wanted to deal with Item 1 where it says what the task is. The task is to prevent the linkage between Mus forces, that is the Muslim armed forces, with the forces from Jablanica in Bijelo Polje. Have you found this?

utterances.speaker: FRANCISCO AGUIRRE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You mean the heading paragraph, before the very first one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, yes, right. And I would like to put to you another question, referring to the same document, item 3.

utterances.speaker: FRANCISCO AGUIRRE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, what do you mean, "another question"? What was the first one?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Again, there is no questions. Counsel is taking us to documents, we are all trying to find the documents and keep up with him, and there are no questions. There has been no question on the last two documents. Are we just leafing through documents now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, let us hear a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have a general question regarding the entire document. How is it relevant to international armed conflict? It speaks about a strictly military operation after the attack on the Northern Camp and it details military tasks, which is to thwart Muslim armed forces and prevent the linkage between their units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: What document are we at now? I'm lost.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm truly sorry. I think we are all a bit tired, and I think I have the hardest time of all. I've been on my feet for an hour and 40 minutes. It's document 492, Your Honour. I hope you have tabs in your binder because I don't. It's Exhibit P492.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: But my question is: If it's not in the binder which was prepared by the Prosecution to show international armed conflict, how can you put a question to this witness? I think you are tired, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because, Your Honour, we have been studying these documents, which the Prosecution is trying to introduce in order to prove international armed conflict, but as far as your last question is concerned, I think you are right, and I think I am mistaken, and I think I have to consult with my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am truly sorry. My colleague has just put me right. So it's Prosecution Exhibit 586, introducing these documents regarding international armed conflict. It's P886. It's a list of documents, and 429 is right there on the first page. It's from the government of B and H.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, Judge Clark's question still applies. How is putting this document to the witness -- we have 17 binders of documents. We can probably spend a lot of time going through 17 binders and putting documents to this witness. This is outside the scope of the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. documents he tendered.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. This is not true, Your Honours. What Mr. Scott just said is simply not true. My colleagues confirmed it. Those are documents related to the UNPROFOR, the government of B and H, the Zagreb archives and the United Nations organisations, which are being tendered or included in these documents. And the numbers go from -- excuse me, Mr. Scott, I'm trying to assist you -- from 241 to 877, of course not in sequence, but the first document is 241 and the last is 877.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Scott, as I understand, that you provided us with lists, the number of the list is P886.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And on this list, that document is listed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Counsel is right on that. I didn't realise, again with all this, that we had changed, that we were moving away from international armed conflict to another subject. With that clarification, I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. You may proceed, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if you approve my suggestion, perhaps we could continue tomorrow. We are really tired and my concentration is failing me. I would have just a couple of more questions for today, and we would continue tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, we just found the right document, and you want us to stop there? Can you -- will you please finish the question concerning the document 492. Then we'll break. Otherwise, tomorrow morning, we won't find our way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've just lost it. Give me a minute, please. Here it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, my question is, if we look at page 2 of this document, item 3, defence of the city of Mostar, it says, "Commander, Brigadier M. Lasic, together with a staff," and the members of the staff are listed. It says, in item 2, it subordinates to the command of the defence of the city of Mostar, the following units. The units are then enumerated. And the list includes the Mostar anti-terrorist group, ATG. I don't understand this part. But it also says, "From the ATG of Tuta." Because it's the first time I come across ATG Mostar and ATG Tuta. And it takes, under its control -- and this order is dated the 2nd of July, 1993, if I got this right, and on the last page, page number 3, the last sentence says, "Pending the execution of these tasks, the following units are directly subordinated to the main staff of the HVO of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna." My question is: Is this document consistent with what you found in the rest of the documentation?

utterances.speaker: FRANCISCO AGUIRRE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm happy to assist you on this point, but I don't think this is related to the issue I was invited to present here, international armed conflict.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, then. I understand. I understand that you have only been invited here to speak to international armed conflict. And my colleague has reminded me just now that the Prosecutor said that these documents, too, will be introduced through you. And that you will provide the foundation for their tendering.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, to avoid -- counsel's correct on that. And as he clarified a moment ago, which I appreciate, there was a second bundle of -- if you'll allow me to use the term "miscellaneous documents" that were tendered through this witness. And I agree, on having a chance to look at it, Exhibit P492 is among those. But it sounds to me that perhaps the witness is under the same confusion I was, that we're still talking about international armed conflict, and this is going to another topic. If the witness can assist us on a proper document authentication question, I don't have any objection to that.

utterances.speaker: FRANCISCO AGUIRRE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: FRANCISCO AGUIRRE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's fine with me. Okay, this document was found in the state archive of Croatia in Zagreb. This is what our records show, and this is what you could see yourselves with the stamp in the first page, on every page, in the upper right part. This is not always the case, but in many cases, it happens. So you can see there. It is my assessment that this is an original document, I mean a photocopy of an original document because the letterhead on the top is the usual Herceg-Bosna and HVO letterhead, because the referenced number where it says in the original number, it says Broj, and then the serial, 02-2 et cetera. This is the original -- a serial number given to the main staff of the HVO, I believe. Beyond that, if we go to the end of the document, we can see that these are -- these stamps of the main staff of the HVO and of the department of Defence are the stamps usually used to Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. put in these documents. As for the signatures, I have not requested a graphologic study of these, but I can tell you at first glance I have seen many documents issued by Milavoj Petkovic with a similar, if not the same, signature. I would say this is actually the signature of Milavoj Petkovic. Then, if you want, we can discuss the credibility of the content in the context of the areas and the period. This is a bit of a more complex discussion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I agree with you; it's a complex discussion, dear colleague. But we have now come to the Croatian state archives, which I wanted to discuss with you to some extent. Is it possible, in view of the fact that this order is three pages long, that somebody inserted page number 1, 2, or 3 with the signatures? Because you found this document in the archives. You don't know where it came from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is pure speculation, ask the witness to speculate if it is possible something could happen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik. Rephrase your question. Or we may break here. We'll resume at 9.30 tomorrow morning.
